meta.description: Competition maths question bank for HK competitions (MathConceptition, HKIMO, SASMO). Year 5-7 level.

questions.text: What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, ___?
What is the next number: 5, 10, 15, 20, ___?
If Monday is Day 1, what day number is Friday?
What is the next number: 1, 3, 5, 7, ___?
questions.solution: These are odd numbers. Each time we add 2. 7 + 2 = 9.

questions.text: Amy is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Carlos. Who is the shortest?
questions.solution: Amy > Ben > Carlos, so Carlos is the shortest.

questions.text: What comes next: 100, 90, 80, 70, ___?
I think of a number. I double it and get 18. What is my number?
questions.solution: If doubling gives 18, the number is 18 ÷ 2 = 9.

questions.text: What is the next number: 3, 6, 12, 24, ___?
Look at this sequence: 2, 6, 18, 54, ___. What is the next number?
In a row of 20 light bulbs, every 3rd bulb is red and every 5th bulb is blue. How many bulbs are both red and blue?
questions.solution: A bulb is both red and blue if its position is a multiple of both 3 and 5, i.e. a multiple of 15. From 1-20, only 15 is a multiple of 15. So 1 bulb.

questions.text: I think of a number. I multiply by 3, then subtract 7, and get 20. What is my number?
What is the 10th term of the sequence: 3, 7, 11, 15, ...?
questions.solution: The rule is: start at 3, add 4 each time. Term n = 3 + (n-1)×4. Term 10 = 3 + 9×4 = 3 + 36 = 39.

questions.text: A frog climbs 3 metres up a pole each day, but slides back 1 metre each night. The pole is 10 metres tall. On which day does the frog reach the top?
questions.solution: Net gain per day = 2m. End of day 1: 2m. Day 2: 4m. Day 3: 6m. Day 4: 8m. Day 5: starts at 8, climbs 3 to 11 — reaches top on day 5.

questions.text: A clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hour and minute hands?
questions.solution: At 3:15, minute hand is at 90°. Hour hand: at 3:00 it's at 90°, and moves 0.5° per minute, so at 3:15 it's at 90 + 7.5 = 97.5°. Angle between = 97.5 - 90 = 7.5°. Rounded to nearest whole = 8°.

questions.text: How many squares are there on a standard 2×2 grid? Count all sizes.
questions.solution: Four 1×1 squares + one 2×2 square = 5 squares total.

questions.text: The sum of three consecutive numbers is 42. What is the largest of the three?
questions.solution: Let the numbers be n, n+1, n+2. Sum = 3n+3 = 42, so 3n = 39, n = 13. The three numbers are 13, 14, 15. Largest is 15.

questions.text: How many squares of all sizes are on a standard 3×3 grid?
A snail climbs 5 metres up a wall each day but slides back 2 metres each night. The wall is 26 metres tall. On which day does the snail reach the top?
questions.solution: Net gain per day = 3m. After day 7: 7×3 = 21m. Day 8: climbs 5m from 21 to 26. Reaches top on day 8 before sliding back.

questions.text: The sum of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 75. What is the middle number?
questions.solution: Five consecutive odd numbers centred on n: n-4, n-2, n, n+2, n+4. Sum = 5n = 75, so n = 15.

questions.text: In a knockout tournament with 32 players, how many matches are needed to find the winner?
questions.solution: Each match eliminates exactly 1 player. To go from 32 to 1 player, we need 31 eliminations = 31 matches.

questions.text: A number leaves remainder 3 when divided by 5 and remainder 2 when divided by 3. What is the smallest such positive number?
questions.solution: Numbers with remainder 3 when ÷5: 3, 8, 13, 18... Numbers with remainder 2 when ÷3: 2, 5, 8, 11... The smallest in both lists is 8.

questions.text: What is the units digit of 7^2026?
questions.solution: Powers of 7 cycle in units digit: 7, 9, 3, 1, 7, 9, 3, 1... Period = 4. 2026 ÷ 4 = 506 remainder 2. So units digit = 2nd in cycle = 9.

questions.text: Anna has some sweets. She gives half to Ben, then gives a third of what remains to Carol. She has 10 left. How many did she start with?
questions.solution: After giving to Carol, Anna has 10. Before Carol: 10 is 2/3 of what she had, so she had 15. Before Ben: 15 is half of what she had, so she started with 30.

questions.text: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add up to 10?
How many squares of all sizes can be found on a standard 8×8 chessboard?
A 4-digit number ABCD is divisible by 9. A=2, B=0, D=3. What is C?
questions.solution: For divisibility by 9: A+B+C+D must be divisible by 9. 2+0+C+3 = 5+C. For this to be divisible by 9, C = 4 (giving 9).

questions.text: The product of two consecutive integers is 2550. What is the larger integer?
What is the sum of all integers from 1 to 100 that are divisible by neither 3 nor 5?
In a room, everyone shakes hands with everyone else exactly once. There are 45 handshakes in total. How many people are in the room?
questions.solution: Number of handshakes = n(n-1)/2 = 45. So n(n-1) = 90. Testing: 10×9 = 90 ✓. There are 10 people.

questions.text: What is the last two digits of 99^99?
questions.solution: 99 = 100-1. 99^99 = (100-1)^99. All terms except the last have factor 100², so only the last term matters for last 2 digits: (-1)^99 = -1. So last two digits of 99^99 end in ...99. Answer: 99.

questions.text: What is 25 × 4?
questions.solution: 25 × 4 = 100. Think of it as four 25s making 100.

questions.text: What is the sum of all digits in the number 2468?
What is 1000 - 367?
How many even numbers are there between 1 and 20 (not including 1 and 20)?
What is 12 × 11?
Round 4567 to the nearest hundred.
questions.solution: 4567 → the tens digit is 6 (≥5), so round up: 4600.

questions.text: What is the smallest 3-digit number?
What is 144 ÷ 12?
How many times does the digit 7 appear when you write all numbers from 1 to 100?
questions.solution: Units place: 7,17,27,37,47,57,67,77,87,97 = 10 times. Tens place: 70-79 = 10 times. Total = 20.

questions.text: What is the LCM (lowest common multiple) of 12 and 18?
The product of two numbers is 96 and their sum is 20. What is the larger number?
questions.solution: We need a×b = 96 and a+b = 20. Testing: 8×12 = 96, 8+12 = 20 ✓. Larger = 12.

questions.text: What is the remainder when 2025 is divided by 7?
How many factors does 36 have?
Anna has 3 times as many stickers as Ben. Together they have 48. How many does Anna have?
questions.solution: Let Ben = b. Anna = 3b. Total: b + 3b = 4b = 48, so b = 12. Anna = 36.

questions.text: What is 999 × 7?
The average of 5 numbers is 24. Four of them are 20, 22, 25, 28. What is the fifth?
questions.solution: Sum of 5 numbers = 5 × 24 = 120. Sum of four = 20+22+25+28 = 95. Fifth = 120-95 = 25.

questions.text: What is the sum of all factors of 60?
How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 50?
A number is divisible by 3, 4, and 5. What is the smallest such positive number?
Anna has 3 times as many stickers as Ben. If Anna gives 12 to Ben, they have equal amounts. How many does Anna start with?
questions.solution: Let Ben = b, Anna = 3b. After: 3b-12 = b+12, so 2b = 24, b = 12. Anna = 36.

questions.text: What is the GCD (greatest common divisor) of 84 and 126?
The digits of a 2-digit number add up to 11. If you reverse the digits, the new number is 27 more than the original. What is the original number?
questions.solution: Let the number be 10a+b. a+b=11. Reversed: 10b+a = 10a+b+27, so 9b-9a=27, b-a=3. From a+b=11 and b-a=3: b=7, a=4. Number = 47.

questions.text: How many 3-digit numbers have all digits different?
questions.solution: First digit: 9 choices (1-9). Second digit: 9 choices (0-9 minus first). Third digit: 8 choices. Total = 9×9×8 = 648.

questions.text: How many zeros are at the end of 50! (50 factorial)?
A 3-digit number ABC is such that ABC = A³ + B³ + C³. One such number is 153. Find another one between 300 and 400.
What is the sum of all 3-digit palindromes?
What is the remainder when 2^100 is divided by 7?
questions.solution: Powers of 2 mod 7 cycle: 2,4,1,2,4,1... Period=3. 100÷3 = 33 remainder 1. So 2^100 mod 7 = 2^1 mod 7 = 2.

questions.text: The number 2^n has 10 digits. What is the smallest possible value of n?
How many sides does a hexagon have?
What is the perimeter of a square with side length 9 cm?
What is the area of a rectangle that is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
How many right angles are there in a rectangle?
questions.solution: A rectangle has 4 right angles (90° each).

questions.text: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.solution: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

questions.text: A circle has a diameter of 14 cm. What is its radius?
What is the sum of angles in a triangle?
questions.solution: The angles in any triangle always add up to 180°.

questions.text: How many faces does a cube have?
A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 cm. Its length is twice its width. What is its area in cm²?
questions.solution: Let width=w, length=2w. Perimeter=2(2w+w)=6w=36, so w=6. Length=12. Area=72 cm².

questions.text: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
A square has an area of 144 cm². What is its perimeter?
Two identical squares overlap to form an L-shape. Each square has side 5 cm and they overlap by a 2×2 square. What is the area of the L-shape?
questions.solution: Total area of two squares = 2×25 = 50. Overlap = 2×2 = 4. L-shape area = 50-4 = 46 cm².

questions.text: A circle has radius 7 cm. What is its circumference? Use π = 22/7.
An isosceles triangle has two sides of length 8 cm and a base of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
How many diagonals does a hexagon have?
A rectangular prism is 4 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm. What is its volume?
A rectangular garden is 20m × 15m. A path 2m wide runs around the inside. What is the area of the path in m²?
questions.solution: Outer area = 20×15 = 300. Inner rectangle = (20-4)×(15-4) = 16×11 = 176. Path area = 300-176 = 124 m².

questions.text: A right triangle has legs of 5 cm and 12 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
A circle has area 154 cm². What is its radius? Use π = 22/7.
Two angles of a triangle are 65° and 45°. What is the third angle?
A cube has total surface area of 150 cm². What is the length of one edge?
What is the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm?
The diagonal of a square is 10 cm. What is the area of the square?
questions.solution: If diagonal = d, then area = d²/2 = 100/2 = 50 cm².

questions.text: A semicircle has diameter 14 cm. What is its perimeter? Use π = 22/7.
questions.solution: Perimeter = half circumference + diameter = πd/2 + d = 22/7 × 14/2 + 14 = 22 + 14 = 36 cm.

questions.text: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. A square is inscribed with one side on the hypotenuse. What is the side length of the square, to 1 decimal place?
questions.solution: Hypotenuse = 10. Height to hypotenuse h = 2×area/10 = 2×24/10 = 4.8. Inscribed square side = (h × hyp)/(h + hyp) = (4.8×10)/(4.8+10) = 48/14.8 ≈ 3.2 cm.

questions.text: How many diagonals does a 12-sided polygon (dodecagon) have?
A cone has radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm. What is its curved surface area? Use π = 3.14.
Two circles have radii 3 cm and 5 cm. The distance between their centres is 10 cm. How many common tangent lines do they have?
questions.solution: Since the distance (10) > sum of radii (8), the circles are separate. Separate circles have exactly 4 common tangents (2 external + 2 internal).

questions.text: A regular hexagon has side length 6. What is its area? Give as an integer (the exact answer is 54√3 ≈ 94).
How many ways can you arrange the letters A, B, C in a row?
questions.solution: 3! = 3×2×1 = 6 ways: ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB, CBA.

questions.text: You have 3 shirts and 2 trousers. How many different outfits can you make?
How many 2-digit numbers can you make using digits 1, 2, 3 (digits can repeat)?
questions.solution: First digit: 3 choices. Second digit: 3 choices. Total = 3 × 3 = 9.

questions.text: In how many ways can you choose 1 book from a shelf of 5 books?
You flip a coin 3 times. How many possible outcomes are there?
How many ways can 4 students line up in a queue?
You have 4 different colours of paint: red, blue, green, yellow. You paint 3 fence posts so no two adjacent posts are the same colour. How many ways?
questions.solution: Post 1: 4 choices. Post 2: 3 (not same as post 1). Post 3: 3 (not same as post 2). Total = 4×3×3 = 36.

questions.text: How many ways can you choose 2 students from a group of 6?
A password is 3 digits long. Each digit is 0-9. How many passwords have all different digits?
How many 3-letter codes can be made from A, B, C, D, E if no letter is repeated?
A pizza shop offers 3 sizes and 4 toppings. Each pizza has exactly 1 size and 1 topping. How many different pizzas can you order?
How many ways can you distribute 3 identical sweets among 2 children?
questions.solution: Child A gets 0,1,2, or 3 sweets (child B gets the rest). That's 4 ways.

questions.text: In how many ways can you arrange 5 people in a circle?
How many ways can you choose 3 students from a group of 8?
You have 5 flags of different colours. How many different signals can you make using exactly 3 flags in a row?
How many 4-digit even numbers can be formed using digits 1,2,3,4,5 without repetition?
questions.solution: Last digit must be 2 or 4 (2 choices). First 3 digits: 4×3×2 = 24 ways. Total = 2×24 = 48.

questions.text: 10 points are marked on a circle. How many triangles can be formed by joining 3 of these points?
How many ways can the letters of MISSISSIPPI be arranged? Give the answer divided by 1000 (rounded down).
questions.solution: MISSISSIPPI has 11 letters: M(1), I(4), S(4), P(2). Arrangements = 11!/(4!×4!×2!) = 39916800/(24×24×2) = 34650. Divided by 1000 = 34.

questions.text: A committee of 5 must be chosen from 6 men and 4 women. The committee must have at least 2 women. How many ways?
How many ways can you climb a staircase of 10 steps if you can take 1 or 2 steps at a time?
In how many ways can 8 identical books be placed on 3 distinct shelves?
A grid is 4×3. How many shortest paths are there from bottom-left to top-right?
questions.solution: Need 4 right + 3 up moves = 7 total. Choose 3 for up: C(7,3) = 35.

questions.text: How many subsets of {1,2,3,4,5,6} contain at least 2 elements?
questions.solution: Total subsets = 2^6 = 64. Subsets with 0 elements = 1. With 1 element = 6. At least 2 = 64-1-6 = 57.

questions.text: 5 couples attend a party. How many ways can 5 people be chosen such that no couple is among the chosen? (Choose 1 from each couple or neither from a couple, total chosen = 5)
questions.solution: From each of 5 couples, choose exactly one person: 2×2×2×2×2 = 32.
